title: Healthy baseline
summary: A steady Contoso Care OLTP mix: front-desk patient lookups, provider schedules, billing balances, check-ins, work-queue triage, supply updates, and audit events. Short, indexed statements with no blocking, used as the baseline activity profile and as the before picture for every incident. On T5 (Cosmos DB), the same steady pace as point reads, upserts, and single-partition queries on patient documents.

intensity.description: Pace: about 1 operation per second per session at 1, about 20 at 10.

notes.T3: Keeps the serverless database awake while it runs; the T3 baseline in activity-profiles.json uses one session at intensity 2.
notes.T4: The PostgreSQL steps (database/postgresql/120-scenario-functions.sql): the same lookups, a work-item touch, and a tagged audit row; the T4 baseline uses one session at intensity 2.
notes.T5: The runner's Cosmos DB REST client, in contosocare/patient-events: 40% point reads, 40% upserts, and 20% single-partition queries over 500 patients (p-0001 to p-0500). Upserts overwrite each patient's profile document and 20 events (hb-ev-0 to hb-ev-19), so storage stays bounded without deletes; the T5 baseline uses one session at intensity 2, a few RU/s against the container's 400.

expectedSymptoms: Short, indexed queries with no blocking and no lock waits
Stable CPU, memory, and IO; Processes blocked stays at 0
A small, bounded number of audit rows written by the workload (trimmed hourly and removed by reset)
queryLevelEvidence: Query Store: many short queries with low duration and logical reads
demo.scenario_runs and demo.scenario_run_events record the run, its sessions, and its counters
T5: ContosoCare.Workload status --target T5 shows the run and its requests, RU, and 429s per second
reset: Status changes toggle within their seeded values, so business data stays as seeded; auto-cleanup and reset remove the workload's audit rows. On T5, upserts overwrite a bounded set of documents, so there's nothing to remove.
